title: Statens Museum for Kunst: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty works at SMK, from a tavern encounter to an empty studio and a face divided by green.
introduction:
A man turns toward the viewer in Carl Bloch's tavern, as though someone has approached the table. In Hammershøi's room, a woman's face remains turned away. These two pictures offer different kinds of access: one produces an encounter, the other gives the room more freely than it gives its inhabitant.

This selection from Copenhagen's SMK follows such differences in looking. Artists examine sketches, clouds and ships under construction; Matisse and Derain ask how strongly colour can change while a face or body remains legible. The twenty works connect through those problems rather than through a single period. Some make observation their subject, while others make the viewer's own position unusually noticeable.
visitNote: The selection comes from SMK’s collection and does not assume that all twenty works are currently displayed. Check the museum’s collection and exhibition information for loans, room changes and individual object availability.

books.title: Concerning the Spiritual in Art
books.author: Wassily Kandinsky; translated by Michael Sadleir
books.note: Kandinsky’s argument about colour gives a historical companion to the Matisse and Derain paintings. His claims are one artist’s position, not a formula for interpreting the older portraits or Hammershøi’s interiors.

works.title: In a Roman Osteria
works.credit: Carl Bloch. In a Roman Osteria. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: The turned head makes the table's company aware of a presence outside the picture. Its near edge brings that encounter close, while other diners continue farther back in the darker room. Bloch gives the scene an implied interruption without showing who has arrived. The viewer occupies the position from which that interruption seems to come.

works.title: The Fall of the Titans
works.credit: Cornelis van Haarlem. The Fall of the Titans. Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen. Public domain; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: The bodies turn in opposing directions, making it difficult to locate a stable position within the fall. Rocks provide points of contact but little security. The mythological defeat also becomes a display of the body's possible twists and extensions, with anatomy supplying the principal means through which collective disaster is made visible.

works.title: Portrait of Madame Matisse: The Green Line
works.catalogueTitle: Portrait of Madame Matisse. The Green Line
works.credit: Henri Matisse. Portrait of Madame Matisse. The Green Line. SMK, Copenhagen. Public Domain Mark 1.0; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: The green band divides the face into differently coloured halves without preventing recognition of Amélie Matisse. Its force comes from contrast rather than naturalistic flesh tones. This is also a small painting, about 40.5 by 32.5 centimetres: the emphatic colour gives it a presence that a screen reproduction can easily confuse with physical scale.

works.title: Pierrot
works.credit: Pierrot (Self Portrait as Pierrot). WikiArt; Amedeo Modigliani. Proportional resizing and JPEG compression; source frame preserved.
works.description: The ruff and angular headwear identify a theatrical role, while the long face is assembled from narrow features and greenish areas. The figure remains human despite its mask-like presentation. Costume therefore provides more than a topic: it allows a portrait-like image to test how far a face can be simplified and still register as a person.

works.title: Portrait of a Man
works.credit: El Greco. Portrait of a man (Andrea Palladio). WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/el-greco/portrait-of-a-man-andrea-palladio-1575
works.description: The pale hand extends beyond the compact dark clothing, giving the portrait an action outside the face. Cuffs and beard remain distinct against the subdued setting. The sitter has sometimes been identified as Palladio, but that name is disputed. The gesture and likeness can be described without turning the proposed identity into a certainty.

works.title: The Wounded Philoctetes
works.credit: Nicolai Abildgaard. The Wounded Philoctetes. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: Both hands draw attention toward the injured foot, while the back and limbs fold around it. Pain becomes an organisation of the whole body rather than something confined to an expression. The figure's isolation makes the act of holding the wound particularly clear: there is no surrounding group to distribute the scene's weight.

works.title: A Group of Danish Artists in Rome
works.catalogueTitle: A Group of Danish Artists in Rome
works.credit: Constantin Hansen. A Group of Danish Artists in Rome. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: The men share a room without sharing a single action. Sitting, standing and turning in different directions gives artistic company the appearance of ongoing occupation rather than a ceremonial assembly. Individual likenesses remain part of a collective portrait, and the open view beyond prevents the room from becoming an entirely sealed professional world.

works.title: View of the Interior of the Colosseum
works.catalogueTitle: View of the Interior of the Colosseum
works.credit: Christoffer Wilhelm Eckersberg. View of the Interior of the Colosseum. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: Arches and broken walls remain parts of a structure whose distances can be followed. The small figures establish a bodily scale without turning the ruin into a setting for a major incident. Eckersberg's account depends on intervals and changing planes, allowing the building's organisation to survive alongside its visible incompleteness.

works.title: View from Dosseringen towards Nørrebro
works.catalogueTitle: A View from Dosseringen near the Sortedam Lake Looking Towards Nørrebro
works.credit: Christen Købke. A View from Dosseringen near the Sortedam Lake Looking Towards Nørrebro. SMK, Copenhagen. Public Domain Mark 1.0; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: The flagpole sets one firm vertical against the broad horizontal continuity of water and sky. Two nearby figures and a distant boat occupy only a small part of that extent. The result is a landscape in which ordinary activity has room without having to become the principal measure of everything around it.

works.title: A Room in Strandgade with the Artist’s Wife
works.catalogueTitle: A Room in the Artist's Home in Strandgade, Copenhagen, with the Artist's Wife
works.credit: Vilhelm Hammershøi. A Room in the Artist's Home in Strandgade, Copenhagen, with the Artist's Wife. SMK, Copenhagen. Public Domain Mark 1.0; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: The woman's face is withheld, while the room's boundaries remain unusually clear. A small grid of sunlight gives the floor a localised event within the larger stillness. The contrast matters: the painting offers precise information about space without offering equivalent access to the person occupying it.

works.title: Interior with the Artist’s Easel
works.credit: Vilhelm Hammershøi. Interior with the Artist’s Easel. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: An easel and a framed picture identify a working space, yet the artist is absent. The open doorway extends the room into another area without introducing visible activity. The arrangement allows painting to become the subject through its equipment and conditions: a place for looking and making remains even when neither is being performed.

works.title: Woman in a Chemise
works.credit: André Derain. Woman in a Chemise. Statens Museum for Kunst, Copenhagen. Public domain; compressed study reproduction.
works.description: The familiar pose—chin supported by a hand—keeps the body legible while pink, blue and green disrupt ordinary distinctions between skin, fabric and shadow. Colour does structural work instead of merely filling an outline. Seen beside Matisse's portrait, the painting offers another way to preserve a figure while changing the hues through which it is recognised.

works.title: The Ryberg Family
works.credit: Jens Juel. The Ryberg Family. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: Gestures link the seated older man with the standing pair, while the landscape gives their family grouping a wider social setting. The distant view is not incidental scenery: it extends their presentation beyond the immediate foreground. The portrait's claim to position therefore depends on land and surroundings as well as likeness.

works.title: Ditlev Blunck Examining a Sketch in a Mirror
works.catalogueTitle: En ung kunstner (Ditlev Blunck) betragter en skitse i et spejl
works.credit: Wilhelm Bendz. En ung kunstner (Ditlev Blunck) betragter en skitse i et spejl. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: The mirror supplies another view of the sketch, making judgment visible as a practical change of vantage point. Tools and canvases crowd around the painter, locating that act within a working room. The image shows looking as part of making: the artist pauses to assess what another orientation may reveal.

works.title: Interior with a Violin
works.credit: Henri Matisse. Interior with a Violin. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: The resting violin gives the interior a sign of use without requiring a musician. Open shutters connect the room to a brighter outside, while dark frames divide its adjoining areas. The instrument and furniture participate in the colour arrangement, so a familiar object can hold attention without becoming the centre of a narrative.

works.title: Concert: The Artist’s Children and Their Playmates
works.credit: Otto Haslund. "Koncert". Kunstnerens børn og deres legekammerater. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: The children bring different kinds of attention to the piano. Some concentrate; others, including the youngest figures, interrupt the idea of a perfectly coordinated concert. That variety makes the gathering more specific than an emblem of domestic harmony. The performance includes the uneven participation that comes with sharing a room across ages.

works.title: A Charlatan Selling Blacking in Piazza Barberini
works.catalogueTitle: A Charlatan Selling Blacking in the Piazza Barberini in Rome
works.credit: Wilhelm Marstrand. A Charlatan Selling Blacking in the Piazza Barberini in Rome. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: The seller's demonstration gathers an audience, making persuasion the activity that joins the figures. Their differing responses matter as much as his gesture. Buildings and fountain locate the event in a Roman square, but the commercial performance supplies the closer structure: attention must be won before a sale can be made.

works.title: Cloudscape, Study
works.credit: Christoffer Wilhelm Eckersberg. A Cloudscape. Study. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: Only a narrow band of ground anchors the cloud layers. The sky must therefore be differentiated internally, through heavier masses and paler openings, rather than treated as one general background. As a study, the picture gives changing atmospheric forms sustained attention without needing a more prominent subject beneath them.

works.title: A Corvette on the Stocks, Copenhagen
works.catalogueTitle: A Corvette on the Stocks. Copenhagen
works.credit: Christoffer Wilhelm Eckersberg. A Corvette on the Stocks. Copenhagen. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: Raised on wooden supports, the hull reveals surfaces that water would normally conceal. The ship is shown under the conditions that make it possible, before the familiar image of a vessel afloat. The framework is consequently essential rather than an obstruction: it explains the physical relation between this large structure and the ground.

works.title: A Blind Man outside His House
works.catalogueTitle: A Blind Man Outside his House
works.credit: Michael Ancher. A Blind Man Outside his House. Statens Museum for Kunst. Public Domain Mark 1.0. Compressed full-frame reproduction.
works.description: The man's lowered head and supported stance locate him beside the building, while bright light extends over the surrounding ground. The title identifies blindness, but it need not become an explanation of his whole presence. The portrait-like attention to posture gives him a place within the landscape rather than reducing him to a contrast with its visibility.

closingSections.title: Change the distance
paragraphs: Compare a whole composition with a closer view of one detail, keeping the object's dimensions in mind. The effect of Matisse's small portrait differs from that of a large scene of tumbling bodies. SMK's catalogue provides useful object records; current display and visiting arrangements should be checked separately.
